insights.concise_text: The commonly held assumption that attention corresponds to word alignments is tested by measuring whether higher consistency between attention and alignment leads to better translations.

triple.subject: commonly held assumption that attention corresponds to word alignments
triple.object: whether higher consistency between attention and alignment leads to better translations

insights.concise_text: The input-feeding model, which uses recurrent attention, achieves a higher BLEU score and uses attentions closer to the human alignments.

triple.subject: input-feeding model
triple.object: non-recurrent attention in BLEU score and closeness to human alignments

insights.concise_text: Because AER only takes the most attended word into account while attention loss considers the entire attention distribution, their agreement for the two systems provides complementary evidence about attention-alignment differences.

triple.subject: AER and attention loss
triple.object: attention-alignment comparison from the most attended word to the entire attention distribution

insights.concise_text: Although the attention for verbs is substantially more inconsistent with word alignments than for nouns, the NMT system translates verbs more accurately than nouns on average.

triple.subject: attention inconsistency with word alignments for verbs
triple.object: the assumption that alignment consistency improves verb translation

insights.concise_text: The low correlation for verbs confirms that attention to other parts of source sentence rather than the aligned word is necessary for translating verbs, consistent with their smaller average word prediction loss.

triple.subject: low correlation for verbs
triple.object: attention to other parts of source sentence rather than the aligned word to be necessary for translating verbs

insights.concise_text: The higher correlation for nouns means consistency of attention with alignments is more desirable, and the concentrated pattern of attention shows training with explicit alignment labels is useful for generating nouns.

triple.subject: higher correlation for nouns
triple.object: training the attention with explicit alignment labels for generating nouns

insights.concise_text: The large portion of attention paid to words other than alignment points captures other relevant information, so training attention with alignments will force the attention model to forget these useful information.

triple.subject: training attention with alignments
triple.object: the attention model to forget useful information from words other than alignment points

insights.concise_text: The most attended roles when translating to verbs include auxiliary verbs, adverbs (including negation), subjects, and objects, supporting that correct translation of verbs requires attention to different parts of the source sentence.

triple.subject: most attended roles when translating to verbs
triple.object: correct translation of verbs to require attention to different parts of the source sentence

insights.concise_text: Nouns have one of the lowest entropies and the attention of NOUN is closest to alignments on average, explaining why attention entropy can measure closeness of attention to alignment for nouns.

triple.subject: low entropy for nouns
triple.object: attention entropy to measure closeness of attention to alignment in the case of nouns

insights.concise_text: Mixed results from chen2016guided, liu-EtAl:2016:COLING, alkhouli-EtAl:2016:WMT motivate a more fine-grained analysis using POS tags, which exhibit some simple syntactic characteristics.

triple.subject: mixed results
triple.object: a more fine-grained analysis of attention using POS tags
